- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in the following period; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true over 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until price stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early decline (first 5–7 days), model often overshoots; adjust downward by 1–2% in first 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next period if sentiment is trending.
- If model forecast is >85% of true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction: subtract 0.5–1.0% per day.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses direction; align forecast with sentiment direction if sentiment shifts >0.2.
